note: Codes: data/mexico_2025_safety.do (Bookmark #4, Q1 2025 Trust in Government) keeps INEGI columns bp4_1_1, bp4_1_2, bp4_1_3 from conjunto_de_datos_ensu_cb_0325.csv (import delimited case(lower)) and reshapes long with item = column name (core model s3 pattern 1, no positional step); code 9 set missing by the Section IV recode ('replace bp4_1_* = . if bp4_1_* == 9 & !(id_year == 2024 & id_quarter == 1)'), i.e. the .do treats 2025 Q1 as a 1-4 quarter. mapping_basis=data_labels: INEGI's 2025 Q1 data dictionary labels BP4_1_1 'Confianza en el Gobierno federal', BP4_1_2 'Confianza en el Gobierno estatal/Gobierno de la CDMX', BP4_1_3 'Confianza en el Gobierno municipal/Gobierno de la alcaldia (CDMX)'; 3/3 agree with questionnaire 4.1 sub-items 1-3. Cross-check (route 9 style): all 3 live item vectors reproduce the raw INEGI 2025 Q1 CSV (23591 rows) after dropping code 9 -- 12/12 item x level counts (bp4_1_1 1/2/3/4 = 4056/11812/4360/3107; bp4_1_2 = 2271/11609/5359/4058; bp4_1_3 = 2239/10461/5309/5280); code 9 = 256/294/302; no blanks, so no skip routing; live 69921 rows, 23481 ids (110 respondents with 9 on all three drop out). Step 3b, 2025 Q1 vs 2024 (checked against each print, the dictionary, catalogos and .do, not assumed): 2025 Q1 keeps the 2024 Q1 CODES (Seccion IV, bp4_1_1..3) but asks the 2024 Q3 QUESTION -- 4.1 'En su opinion, cuanta confianza le genera...' about three levels of government on the 4-point Mucha confianza..Mucha desconfianza scale -- NOT 2024 Q1's 0-10 'cuanto confia en' about three office-holders. Section title changed to 'CONFIANZA EN LOS NIVELES DE GOBIERNO' (2024 Q3 Seccion V: 'CONFIANZA EN LA ADMINISTRACION PUBLICA'), and 2025 Q1 adds a read-aloud introduction CP3 that neither 2024 print carries. Stem, 3 sub-items and 4 options are string-identical to batch_682's 2024 Q3 shipped Spanish (all 9 shipped Spanish strings found verbatim in the p.5 text layer, checked against a 150 dpi render); catalogos bp4_1_1..3 labels identical to the print. Words: instructions = CP3 read-aloud text (printed 'CP3: A continuacion, le voy a preguntar sobre la confianza que le pueden generar los diversos niveles de gobierno.', the 'CP3:' label stripped); it is the only framing text for the table's one section, so it goes in instructions, not section_prompt. section_prompt = 4.1 stem; item_text = sub-items 1-3. Kept as printed: trailing '?', '(CDMX)', the stem's '...'. Normalised: the render's wider gap in 'Mucha  desconfianza' (justification) shipped with one space, as batch_682 did. Stripped: question/sub-item numbers, dot leaders, |__| entry boxes, interviewer direction 'REGISTRE EL CODIGO CORRESPONDIENTE A CADA OPCION', and the closing CP4 script on the same page. Options: 1-4 printed; 9 'No sabe / no responde' has no row (set missing by the .do). Every level each item's respondents used has an option row (12/12). Dictionary: Description ('Public trust in government institutions to address security concerns, Q1 2025') overstates it -- 4.1 has no security framing; Reference names 'ENSU 2023' while data and wording are the 2025 Q1 wave (file suffix 0325) -- same defect as the siblings. English in _translated is this project's own translation (machine_translation): section_prompt, item_text and option_text English reused verbatim from batch_682 (Spanish identical string for string); instructions_translated (CP3) translated fresh. INEGI publishes no English questionnaire.
public_note: Fuente: INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Seguridad Pública Urbana (ENSU) 2025, primer trimestre -- IRW transcribed Section IV (question 4.1 and its read-aloud introduction) from INEGI's questionnaire, stripped interviewer directions, and added an English translation of its own; INEGI does not endorse this item text. Code 1 is the most trust (Mucha confianza) and 4 the least; the items share codes bp4_1_1..3 with the 2024 first-quarter table but not its question or its 0-10 scale.
